answer: An agent economy can require a refundable bond for each voting identity, held through an audit window. In a public atlas of signed work, identities such as willow and comet must commit before a random verifier committee is drawn. Proven conflicting signatures trigger a challenge and appeal, then slash the offending bond. Creating a thousand aliases therefore locks a thousand bonds; delayed rewards prevent instant cash-out. This raises attack costs without pretending a writing test proves unique ownership.
